title: OrderbookSnapshot
description: One depth snapshot for one instrument on one venue. A DIRECT CONTRACT FOR data.orderbook (instrument_id, venue_id, at, depth, bids, asks, source) with PK (instrument_id, venue_id, at), where both sides are stored as jsonb arrays of [price, size] pairs. That pair-of-numbers form is a boundary encoding, not canonical data: a level's price is a price and its size is a quantity, so a consumer reading the raw array must not treat the numbers as binary64 money. depth records how many levels were requested, which is what makes a truncated snapshot distinguishable from a thin book - the two look identical without it.

at.description: When the book was read. Part of the PK, matching data.orderbook.

$ref.description: How many levels were requested. Without it a truncated snapshot is indistinguishable from a thin book.

level.description: [price, size] as decimal STRINGS, the boundary encoding data.orderbook stores as jsonb. Strings, not numbers, so precision survives the round trip.
